action: Start the scan in the transverse orientation. Place the transducer just above the suprapubic area and aim the beam into the pelvis.
interpretation: Identify the bladder as the primary landmark.
Use the bladder to establish anatomical bearings.

action: Scan away from the bladder to the adjacent tissue.
interpretation: Identify the uterus, visualized just adjacent to the bladder.

action: Sweep continuously through the uterine tissue.
interpretation: Search for the presence of an intrauterine pregnancy.
Look for early signs such as a yolk sac. Visualize fetal heart tones present within the sac.

action: Complete the transverse scan. Rotate the probe to the second axis with the indicator pointing toward the patient's head. Perform a longitudinal sweep.
interpretation: Obtain a second axis view. Inspect the uterus to ensure there is no second gestational sac (Twin B) present.
